verdict.rationale: Amplitude documents Experiment management APIs that programmatically control flags and experiments, and display holdout and mutex groups, so an agent can read experiment configuration. An official MCP server and an OpenAPI spec also exist. Nothing in the evidence shows programmatic access to experiment results, metrics or statistical significance, which an agent needs to summarize outcomes and recommend ship or rollback. missing for 10: documented results/analysis API (metrics, significance, variant performance), evidence that the MCP server exposes experiment data, independent or hands-on corroboration of agent use.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can read experiment configurations and results programmatically to summarize outcomes and recommend ship/rollback decisions

citations.quote: Use the Experiment management API to programmatically create and control flags and experiments.
Manage flags, experiments, and deployments from CI, scripts, or your own tools with the Experiment APIs.
Holdout APIs to create, edit, and display holdout groups and their properties.
official MCP server documented at https://amplitude.com/mcp-server
